items.title: The Early Years: What They Left Out of Joseph Smith’s Official Story
items.summary: A Mormon News Roundup YouTube episode examining Joseph Smith’s early life in 1820s New York, including folk magic, an 1826 trial, and differing accounts of the First Vision, drawing on historical records.

items.title: Brother of key LDS apostle will spend the rest of his life in prison for sending sexually explicit letters to Utah girl
items.summary: The Salt Lake Tribune reports that Wade Christofferson, brother of apostle D. Todd Christofferson, was sentenced to 45 years in federal prison in Ohio after pleading guilty to coercing and enticing a minor. The Tribune says he admitted in plea documents to sexually abusing two girls in Ohio and Utah.

items.title: Former Chicago-area Mormon leader is sentenced to 45 years in prison in child sex abuse case in Ohio
items.summary: The Chicago Sun-Times reports that Wade Christofferson, a former Crystal Lake-area Latter-day Saint leader, was sentenced to 45 years in prison in a federal case in Ohio. The Sun-Times says he was secretly excommunicated for abuse in the 1990s and quickly restored, according to interviews, and that church leaders allegedly covered up earlier misconduct.

items.title: On Tattoos
items.summary: A By Common Consent post asks why the LDS Church strongly discourages tattoos but takes no official position on elective cosmetic surgery, arguing the two are broadly similar. The author discusses the church’s For the Strength of Youth guidance.

items.title: BYU medical school celebrates milestone with drone show
items.summary: The BYU Daily Universe reports the BYU School of Medicine marked its preliminary accreditation on Nov. 13 with a celebration that included a drone show. The school will welcome its first class of up to 60 students in July 2027.

items.title: LDS voters may have even outpaced the blue wave in some congressional races
items.summary: KJZZ interviews Salt Lake Tribune religion reporter Tamarra Kemsley, who says evidence suggests Latter-day Saint voters moved left in the midterms, though how that compares with the broader blue wave is still being sorted out.
